To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ALOX5 gene downregulation in cardiomyocytes protects against anoxia-reperfusion and ischemia-reperfussion injury.
silencing ALOX5 gene in cardiomyocytes and in vivo in rat model of heart I/R results in a reduced cell death and decreased size of myocardial infarct, respectively.
silencing of ALOX-5 protects heart cells from anoxia-reperfusion injury in vitro and from ischemia-reperfusin injury in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of ALOX gene silencing as a cardioprotective strategy.
the development of RNAi as a novel strategy for treatment of heart diseases.
a potential application of ALOX 5 gene silencing for the treatment of myocardial infarctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALOX5 gene is an important target in RNAi-based cardioprotection.
the ALOX5 gene is a potential target for RNAi application to prevent myocardial infarctions and to reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases.
the ALOX5 gene is an attractive target for the treatment of myocardial ischemia-reperfusions injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALOX5 gene silencing by RNA interference protects heart cells against AR and IR injury.
5-lipooxygenase gene (5-LOX) silencing protects heart cells against anoxia/reoxygenation and ischemia/reperfusion injury.
ALOX5 gene silencing protects heart against IR damage by reducing the number of necrotically died cardiomyocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNAi targeting of a single gene can have cardioprotective effect in vivo.
ALOX5 gene silencing is a potential strategy to protect the heart against IR injury.
the 5-lipoxygense gene appears to be an important target for RNAi-based therapeutic approaches in the treatment of myocardial infarctions.
